correctness.rationale: Independently substituted the exact two-product multiplication and the even matrix into all 16 ordered basis-pair identities over the integral polynomial ring. The (f2,f2) torsion forces r=0 in the radical; the remaining generators are (a-s)(p-s), c(p-s), c(a+d-2p), and bc+(d-p)^2. In a prime containing these generators, either c belongs to the prime, forcing d=p and then a=s or s=p, or c does not, forcing s=p and a+d=2p. Conversely the three displayed component ideals contain the torsion ideal. They are incomparable primes over every field extension: the first two define affine four-spaces and the third is the product of an affine plane and the geometrically irreducible cone bc+t^2=0, primitive linear in b over K[c,t]. The sums of any two component ideals give the same affine three-space. The cone has Q(Q-1)+Q points by splitting c nonzero versus zero. The three determinant restrictions independently simplify to a^2 p^2, a p^3, and p^4; the intersection is invertible exactly when p is nonzero. Inclusion-exclusion gives both stated counts. None of the reasoning divides by 2.
residual_risks: This is the reduced even locus, not a claim about nilpotent scheme structure, odd maps, or classification up to conjugacy. The finite-field formulas follow from the component proof, not from running the supplied small-field tests.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural invariant of the smallest explicit motivating product specimen under review, not a chosen slice of a known locus: it turns a verified diagonal family and acknowledged non-exhaustive construction into an all-field operator classification. The coexistence of two affine components with a cone component glued along the same affine subspace, and the invertibility stratification over finite fields, give substantive information not obtainable by counting the known examples.
residual_risks: No minimality among graded algebras and no classification for other perm superalgebras, Nijenhuis scheme structures, or bialgebra constructions are inferred.
